notes: Fixed by kb/Work PB5805. §1985:VII.4.7.3 SR5 ("Integer-1 may be positive or zero, but must not be negative") allows zero; §1985:III.2 makes every integer of a general format "neither signed nor zero unless explicitly allowed by the rules for that format", and SR5 allows no sign (where 1985 allows one it says so, §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR6). SequentialIoBinder.ScreenAdvancingCount admits an integer literal only when NumericLiteral.IsUnsignedForm holds, so +3, +0, -0 and -1 draw COBOL2365 (its text cites the 1985 rules at --std 85), and 0, 3 and ZERO compile (ZERO is a numeric literal of value zero by §1985:IV.4.2.2.2). The 1985 case pb5805-write-advancing-plus-sign-85 refuses +0.
